label: Organizational capacity
description: Demonstrate that the organization has the staff, governance, and history to execute the proposed work.

scoring.desc: Capacity is asserted without evidence or the organization has no relevant track record.
Capacity is described with some staffing and governance detail but key roles are unfilled or unproven.
Capacity is documented with named staff, relevant prior awards, and board oversight appropriate to the award size.

common_failures: Boilerplate staff bios that do not tie to project roles
No mention of board or fiscal oversight
Relying on volunteers for critical delivery without contingency

label: Project feasibility
description: Show the project can be completed within the proposed timeline, budget, and scope using realistic methods.

scoring.desc: Timeline or method is vague and key dependencies are unaddressed.
Timeline and method are plausible but one or two major risks are not mitigated.
Timeline, method, milestones, and risk mitigations are explicit and internally consistent.

common_failures: No contingency for Alaska weather or shipping delays
Scope expansion beyond the award budget

label: Community impact
description: Describe measurable impact on Alaska communities that the project will create.

scoring.desc: Impact is vague or not measurable.
Impact is specific but affects a small population or lacks baseline data.
Impact is specific, measurable, and affects a significant Alaska population with a clear theory of change.

label: Budget appropriateness
description: Show that requested funds are reasonable, allowable, and matched to the scope of work.

scoring.desc: Budget is a lump sum with no line items or contains unallowable costs.
Budget has line items but unit costs or justifications are thin.
Budget ties every line to a project activity with reasonable unit costs and a clear match or leverage story.

common_failures: Indirect rate not stated or not justified
Personnel hours that do not reconcile with the work plan
